(Order on Criminal Misc. Bail Application)

1. Heard Sri Santosh Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the appellants in both the matters and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

This bail application on behalf of accused-appellants convicted and sentenced in S.T. No. 77 of 2014 (State of U.P. Vs. Nathuram), arising out of Case Crime No. 471 of 2012, under Section 302,
364, 201 I.P.C. as well as S.T No. 149 of 2017 (State of U.P. Vs. Brijesh), arising out of Case Crime No. 471 of 2012, under Section 302, 201 119, 120B I.P.C., Police Station Shikohabad, District Firozabad.
3.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the appellants are innocent and have been falsely roped in this case due to suspicion.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the accused-appellants that Nathuram and Brijesh Kumar are in jail since 31.08.2022 and learned counsel further submitted thatappellants have every hope of success in appeal and they undertake that they will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall remain present before the Court as and when required and they will cooperate with the hearing of appeal for which their counsel will remain present on the dates of listing.
4.

Sri Patanjali Mishra, learned A.G.A appearing in Criminal Appeal No. 6938 of 2022 and Sri Goswami, learned A.G.A. appearing in Criminal Appeal No. 6798 of 2022 for the State has vehemently objected to the grant of bail of the accused-appellants.
5. Can conviction be based on apprehension.
The cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence is that the chain in circumstantial evidence case should not have any discrepancy.
The corpus is yet not been recovered for such a long time.
The accident is of the year 2012 where the paramour of the deceased was facing trial under Section 376 I.P.C.

Can it be said that on his statement on or an apprehension that there was a confessional statement to him by the appellant of doing away of their daughter and sister for the alleged elopement/love affair.
Learned judge has convicted the accused.
We are convinced that this is a case which requires consideration and the accused be set free as they were even enlarged on bail during pendency of the trial.
6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, we direct release of the accused-appellants on bail.
Hence, on re-appreciation of material on record, the accused-appellants- Nathuram and Brijesh Kumar, are entitled to be released on bail.

7. We, therefore, direct the jail authorities concerned to release accused-appellants Nathuram and Brijesh Kumar convicted and sentenced in the aforesaid Sessions Trial be released on bail during the pendency of the appeal subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The appellants shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any unnecessary adjournment.
Nathuram vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118686049/
2
(ii)) The appellants shall not leave India without permission of this Court.
(iii) The appellants shall inform the change of address within 10 days, failing which the State shall be at liberty to request for cancellation of his bail.

8. As far as fine is concerned, the entire fine shall remain suspended till final disposal of the appeal,
if yet not deposited.
(Order on Appeal) Office to prepare paper-book.
List the matter when it turn comes.
